messages.author: 9ce51fd941c236e0
messages.subject: [RODBC] ERROR
parts:
Hello;

In our R-Web application, I am trying to fetch data out of oracle through RODBC.
I checked the ODBC connection through iusql - It is working fine.

But this is getting us the following error:
 
> require(RODBC)
> ch <- odbcConnect("DSN", "UID", "PW")
Warning messages:
1: In odbcDriverConnect("DSN=XXX;UID=XXXXXX;PWD=XXXXX") :
  [RODBC] ERROR: state 01000, code 0, message [unixODBC][Driver Manager]Can't open lib '/usr/lib/oracle/11.2/client/lib/libsqora.so.11.1' : file not found
2: In odbcDriverConnect("DSN=XXX;UID=XXXXXX;PWD=XXXXX") :
  ODBC connection failed

File is right there at the mentioned location.
Any thoughts on that? Any help is truly appreciated.

Thanks,
Rachit

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: [RODBC] ERROR
parts:
Hi Rachit,

I would suspect that there are Oracle environment variables not being
set when running your application in apache. Typically, shell users
would source an oracle_env.sh file prior to connecting with command
line applications (R included).

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: [RODBC] ERROR
parts:
Thanks for your kind help. Sorry, it took me some time to look into the issue in more detail.
When I am using 'R' as root to get into R and try to access data out of Oracle, everything is working fine.

That's strange that If I use 'sudo R' as root and try to access the data out of Oracle, it is getting me the following error:
[RODBC] ERROR: state 01000, code 0, message [unixODBC][Driver Manager]Can't open lib '/usr/lib/oracle/11.2/client/lib/libsqora.so.11.1':file not found
Now when I am using the same code in my web application, I am getting the same error through web browser:
[RODBC] ERROR: state 01000, code 0, message [unixODBC][Driver Manager]Can't open lib '/usr/lib/oracle/11.2/client/lib/libsqora.so.11.1' : file not found

How to overcome this? I thought there are any permission/user rights that are supposed to set up.
I tried many such ways with no success. Can anyone provide any direction where I should move ahead?

Thanks,
Rachit
